doc.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21

title: Underage in the district: cops, food and poison fears
summary: Pops dodged the corner cops as an underage player; King Oliver and his brother warned him about food sent by a woman. Mugsy starts asking a newcomer about Chicago.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: And I said, Louie, did you get them?

Yeah. I said, Louie, did you get them? Yeah. I said, well you had two. I went to the toilet, I stopped the toilet. See I couldn't go. Once I go in the cavalry, I had to stay in there. Because the cops would chase me. Because I was underage, I ain't got no business down there. But my boys being a good family. You're supposed to be 21 to work there, huh? Yeah. See I could go on one side of the street, but the cops on this corner knowed me. See you had two cops here, two cops here, two cops over there, two cops over there. Each corner? Each corner? Yeah. Well these two cops know me, and these two cops know me. But when I go in there like to stay in there like to want Each quarter? Two cops, yeah. Well these two cops normally, these two cops normally here. When I go in there, when I go in the stadium, like I want a sandwich or anything, I had to send out somebody. I had a little chick. Used to send me my food. And King Oliver and my brother, man, they boys hit me for a long time. Don't eat that, man. That woman's trying to trick you, man. She's going to poison you. See? He said, you know, if they fix it for you, if we, they just don't even hurt us. That's right, Willie. I said, man, they eat all the food, you can drink the milk. She can't put nothing in milk. They let me drink the milk and eat all that food for a long time. Tell Eddie Grocer, my boss, Foster, it's a nice food. She'll come in. I said, yeah. I said, but Joe didn't tell me. Don't eat it. My brother says, because a woman can fix something for you. I said, my daddy, I said, can a woman do you anything? If she put something in for me and you eat it, don't want to hurt you. He said, hell yeah, if she puts something in for you it'll kill me too. He said, what the hell are they doing to you, Joe? I said, they tell me you don't eat it. What you don't eat of that boy? What you eat of your food? From then on I used to eat my food. But that ought to have been going on for months, you know. Does he? Don't eat it. And all the guys, and all the guys, all the dude for that. Yeah, man. Do that, man. You know, I wouldn't want to tell your mother that you got sick on a woman giving something to eat on that man, and they ain't going to hurt us. They all eat it man, she sent me big steak, fried chicken and stuff, there's something to eat later, and I'd be looking at it. And they'll, I'll get you a hamburger, Joe, I'm going to go outside and get me two hamburgers. I said, well I've got steak and chicken, they'll send me there for me. Boy, it came out and he said to me, my brother, my brother laughed at it right now, he said to me, he was right in the window with him too, helping me. He sent me a bottle of milk and a bottle of whiskey. See, I have a 2.15 apartment.

Oh yeah? Well let's, let's, well you know, we can all join in. Yeah. How did you first start, Rosie? Well I started on Clark Street, Chicago, just when I was a kid going to school. Are you a, are you a Chicagoan? Yes, I'm born and raised in Chicago. I didn't know the north side. Everyone thinks I was raised in the south side, but I wasn't. It'd be right up south side. I used to live on the south side and I had music, Joe Alvarez. Who were the first people you heard on the south side? Joe Alvarez. Joe Alvarez. No, Joe Alvarez wasn't the first one. Jelly Roll and. Manuel. Dominic. Yeah, Manuel, you heard Manuel from you, Johnny. Yeah, I heard that. Manuel Perez was up there for Donny.
